evidence: Version 2 (image 6) resolves the Board-formed Sea Wall Ledger more completely: the wall reads as cast panels with horizontal formwork seams plus vertical panel joints and evenly spaced round tie marks, the honed ground plane carries a soft tonal gradient and a believable receding perspective, and the bottle's base settles into it with a soft matte contact shadow consistent with the diffuse sea-fog light. The left Times column is cleaner here: DAVIDOFF at column head, 'Cool / Water' across two tall serif lines with generous leading, EAU DE TOILETTE and the short slate tide-gauge rule closing the column, all with wide horizontal clearance from the bottle shoulder. The product cutout stays faithful (opaque black cap, luminous ocean-blue slab, crisp white print) and sits right of centre within the safety bounds. Version 1 (image 5) is close but weaker: its wall shows only a single horizontal seam with sparse tie marks so the board-formed ledger rhythm is thin, the floor plane is flatter and reads more like a pasted band, the contact shadow is fainter so the bottle grips the cement less convincingly, and the column's slate rule and EDT line sit slightly tighter against the tie-mark rows, muddying the calm left wall the concept demands.
remaining_problems: Contact shadow under the bottle in version 2 is still very soft and slightly uniform; a touch more density at the base line would anchor the packshot further into the honed ground.
The vertical panel joints in the wall introduce a grid the brief's purely horizontal board rhythm did not ask for, mildly competing with the horizontal tide-gauge logic of the type column.
The slate rule and EAU DE TOILETTE line float with a large vertical gap below the serif title, leaving the column's middle slightly under-weighted.

Cool sea-fog light is convincing on the cement but the glass body keeps a studio-style internal glow with little environmental reflection from the pale ground, so material dialogue between cement and glass remains mostly tonal rather than optical.
